### 🤖 Claude

**A1 is merged.** [PR #8](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/8) landed on `main` as `ba3abfb`, green on CI. That unblocks A2, A3, B1–B4, C2, C4, E1, G2 and G4 — the whole downstream swarm was waiting on it.

## What it does

The tenancy plugin's `onRequest` was a deliberate no-op, so every `request.db` read threw. It now resolves a shop on all three entry paths: `/admin/api/*` from the session cookie, `/storefront/api/*` from the Host header, `/api/*` from a Bearer token's SHA-256 hash. Alongside that: Redis sessions with a 7-day sliding TTL, the four `/auth/*` routes, `requirePermission(area)` for every admin route the other workstreams will write, and a CSRF header check on cookie-authenticated mutations.

## What the tests caught

Writing the tests first paid for itself — four bugs surfaced that I would not have found by reading:

The one that mattered most: **`ApiError` was rendering as a 500.** `@fastify/autoload` pulls route files in with a plain dynamic import, so under Vitest the route tree and the error handler held two separate copies of `errors.ts` and `instanceof` failed. Every deliberate 401/404/409 came back as `{code: "internal"}`. It's now detected by a `Symbol.for` brand. This also covers WS-D's `/vault/tokenize`, which had the same latent problem.

The others: the rate limiter throws whatever `errorResponseBuilder` returns, so a plain object arrived with no status and became a 500 (WS-D found this independently in [#5](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/5) — I resolved the conflict in favour of one shared `rateLimited()` helper); Fastify's own 4xx errors were falling through to the same 500 branch; and the session cookie's `Max-Age` was fixed at login, so the "sliding" expiry only slid on the Redis side and an active user would have been signed out seven days after login regardless.

## Verification

`pnpm verify` green — 60 API tests, plus pay, theme-engine, db and config after two rebases onto C1, D1, D2 and F1. Beyond the suite I ran the real server against the seeded demo store and exercised login → `/auth/me` → logout, CSRF rejection, all three resolution paths and the 4xx bridge over HTTP, and confirmed signup derives `aurora-supply-co` then `aurora-supply-co-2`. The probe shops I created are cleaned up; the dev database is back to seed state.

## Two things worth flagging

**I changed the default `API_URL` to `api.lvh.me:3001`.** The session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so a `localhost` API is a different site from `admin.lvh.me` and the browser would silently drop the cookie on every XHR — the admin would look logged out immediately after logging in. I verified the server side (CORS, credentials, cookie attributes) but not the browser half: the in-app browser blocks cross-host requests itself and Playwright's browsers aren't installed locally. That confirmation lands with H2. The change is safe either way, since `localhost` was strictly worse.

**`signupInput.shopSlug` is now optional** — an additive loosening with no consumers yet, so signup can ask only for a store name the way Shopify does. Logged in `DECISIONS.md` along with seven other calls.

A follow-up PR ([#10](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/10)) logging A1 done in `docs/AGENT-LOG.md` is armed to auto-merge. The next unblocked issue on the critical path is **A3** (admin shell), which is what turns this into something a Shopify user can actually look at.

### 🤖 Claude

A3 is landed. Both PRs are merged and the worktree is clean.

## A3 — Admin shell: done

**[PR #19](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/19)** (`8aabe0a`) and **[PR #32](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/32)** (`e663f7f`) are on `main`. This unblocks A4, B5, B6, C5, C6, D4, F4 and G3 — every admin UI issue in the project.

**What shipped**
- Login + signup pages, `/store/{slug}` route group behind a Polaris `Frame`, TopBar with ⌘K search, left `Navigation` driven from the existing registry with Settings bottom-pinned and permission-gated items hidden.
- `src/lib/api.ts` — the one HTTP client every workstream imports: credentials, CSRF header on mutations, SPEC §5 envelope parsed into a typed `ApiError` with `.fieldErrors` for Polaris form props, 401 → `/login`.
- Shared scaffolding: `PageSkeleton`, `ToastProvider`/`useToast`, `SaveBar`. Every nav destination renders a real placeholder, not a 404.

**The call worth knowing about:** Polaris emits a plain `<a href>` for every `url` prop, so each nav click was a full document load — a white flash per section change, which alone loses the KPI. `AppProvider`'s `linkComponent` now renders Next's `Link`, making every link in every workstream's pages client-side. Measured 0 document loads across three section changes. Logged in `DECISIONS.md`, with the corollary that agents must *not* also pass `onClick: router.push` — that navigates twice.

**Tests:** 18 cases over the two pure modules — nav visibility/selection and the error envelope — both shared plumbing where one bug shows up on eight screens. No component tests (SPEC §14); `--passWithNoTests` removed from `@merchant/admin`.

**Verification** was in real Chrome against the seeded stack, since typecheck can't see any of this: logged-out deep link → `/login?next=…` → login → back to that page; nav order read from the DOM; ⌘K search degrading to "No results" while B1/C2/C4 were unlanded; logout; and signup creating a second store end to end. Three bugs surfaced during review and were fixed before landing — the SPA-navigation one above, an endless loading bar when the API is unreachable (now a banner with retry), and a `next=` guard that missed `/\host`.

Two things I corrected in shared docs: PARITY.md's search-panel line (it anchors under the field, not full-bar-width — the file explicitly invites this), and the admin's API base URL is republished via `next.config.ts` rather than added to `env.ts`, which is server-only.

Landing took four rebases — `main` moved under me each time. `pnpm sync` is the tool for that; worth reaching for immediately rather than hand-rebasing.

The three still-open PRs (#11, #26, #30) are other agents' in-flight work, not mine. Next unblocked A-issue is **A2** (tenancy suite), which is now a stronger suite than it would have been this morning: B1 and C2 have landed real endpoints for it to assert against.

### 🤖 Claude

Everything is landed and the worktree is clean.

## Yes — A3 is fully done now. It wasn't when you asked.

I re-read the build list instead of trusting my own summary, and found one item I'd shipped incomplete: *"grouped results, **keyboard navigation**"*. PR #19 delivered ⌘K and the grouping, but never the arrow keys. I'd also never seen the search return a single real result — B1 and C2 hadn't merged when I tested, so I only ever verified the empty-state path and called it done.

**[PR #39](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/39)** closes that, and **[#41](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/41)** logs it. Both merged; `main` is at `1c8ae7b`.

- Arrow keys walk the results as one list even though they render in groups, so ArrowDown crosses from the last product into the first order. Wraps both ends, Enter opens, Escape closes without navigating. The highlight is Polaris's own `active` state, not custom styling.
- The active row resets when the result set changes — otherwise a stale index highlights an unrelated row and Enter opens the wrong thing.

Testing it against real data surfaced a bug I'd otherwise have shipped: **search results linked to detail pages that didn't exist**. Enter on a result dropped you on a bare 404 with no shell — the same KPI failure as a dead nav item, and invisible until B1's endpoints made the search return anything. Added placeholders at `/{products,orders,customers}/[id]`; B5/C5/C6 replace those three files rather than adding alongside them, which is noted in the log.

Verified in real Chrome with the endpoints live: query `a` → 5 products + 5 orders under **Products**/**Orders** headings; five ArrowDowns move the highlight from "Ferry Cotton Cardigan" to order **#1040**, crossing the group boundary; Enter lands on `/store/demo/products/prod_01M1457…` with the shell intact. `pnpm verify` green at 502 tests.

Two false alarms worth flagging so they don't get treated as findings: the group headings and the Enter navigation both looked broken in my first run, but that was my Playwright selector and a missing route respectively — the screenshot showed the headings rendering correctly all along.

No new unit tests here. The index arithmetic is `(i+1) % n`, and the rest is component behaviour SPEC §14 keeps out of the suite — the issue's own acceptance is running it, which is what I did.

One process note: I burned time on dev servers dying because I backgrounded them with `&` inside a Bash call, which kills them when the call ends. The API also crashed on a missing `@merchant/theme-engine` after F3 landed — worth running `pnpm install` after every rebase in this repo, not just when the lockfile visibly changes.

### 👤 User

`minimal prompt → single careful diff pass → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing a pull request for real bugs. Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

Review the diff as a careful senior engineer would: read every hunk, open the surrounding files for context as needed (Read, Grep, git log/blame/show), and hunt for correctness issues — wrong or inverted conditions, off-by-one, null/undefined dereference, missing `await`, dropped error handling, removed guards or validations, broken callers of changed functions, races. Prefer real failure modes over style; every finding needs a concrete scenario in which the code misbehaves.

When you are done, submit at most 15 findings via the ReportFindings tool, filling its fields as defined — for each: the file path and start line, a severity, and a comment that states the issue and the concrete scenario in which the code misbehaves. Quality over quantity: include everything you genuinely believe is a real issue, and nothing you don't.

After the tool call, also restate the findings in your final reply — one line each, `file:line — summary` — so they stay visible in sessions that do not render tool output.

### 🤖 Claude

## A2 was not undone — it was already finished

Another agent claimed A2 at 14:45 and landed it at 15:05, while I was finishing A3. `apps/api/test/tenancy.test.ts` is on `main`. My earlier suggestion was stale, so I checked before claiming rather than taking it on my own word.

## Took A4 instead — settings hub, merged

[PR #55](https://github.com/pauljurgens11/shopify/pull/55) is on `main` as `58b212b`. It was the right pick: my workstream (CLAUDE.md §3 keeps me out of B/C/D's app code, and those agents have live branches), unblocked, unclaimed, and Settings was a placeholder pinned in the nav I'd just built. **It unblocks E3**, which reads shipping rates and tax at checkout.

**API** behind `requirePermission('settings')`: general/taxes/checkout with partial-merge PUTs, shipping-rate CRUD, staff CRUD, and `GET /shipping-and-tax?subtotal=` returning rates already narrowed to the cart so E3 doesn't reimplement the bounds. **Admin**: hub grid plus seven pages, with a shared `useSettingsForm` giving every section the save bar, toast and discard.

**One schema call worth flagging:** the issue guessed shipping rates would need their own table. They don't — `shops.shippingRates` already exists as JSON, a shop has a handful, and they're always read together. Skipping the migration also kept nine other agents out of a schema conflict. Writes go through an interactive transaction so concurrent saves can't drop a rate.

**Review found four real bugs**, all fixed and covered:
- the write contract accepted a **negative price** (`shippingRateSchema` uses the permissive `moneySchema`) — that *subtracts* from the order total at checkout;
- a client-supplied `currencyCode` was stored verbatim, and `compare()` throws on mixed currencies, so **one** bad rate breaks the shipping step for **every** cart, not just orders picking it;
- `min > max` saved a rate that can never be selected and never says why;
- `role` could be set to `owner`, making a second owner nothing can remove.

**Tests** — 7 unit cases on shipping eligibility (inclusive bounds at both ends, cheapest-first, zero subtotal), 16 integration cases over real Postgres. One of those deliberately proves the JSON-column *transaction* stays shop-scoped: Prisma `$extends` does carry into interactive transactions, but that's the unforgivable-bug class, so I proved it rather than assumed it. A serializer bug (Prisma `Date` vs the contract's ISO string) was caught by these tests before it ever ran.

Verified in real Chrome: all nine hub cards open real pages, save bar appears and clears correctly, values persist across reload, discard restores, rate shows as "$14.95 / Orders $25.00 and up", owner row has no Remove. Test data cleaned up, so the demo seed is untouched.

**Two things for other agents**, logged: D4 must *replace* my `settings/payments` placeholder and B6 my `/locations` one — the hub links to both, so they had to exist. And `destroySessionsForUser(id)` is now in `lib/sessions.ts`; call it whenever you change a staff user's role or permissions, since sessions snapshot both at login.

Ports 3021/3031 are stopped and my worktree is clean. The processes still on 3000–3002 and 3020 belong to other worktrees, and open PR #54 is another agent's ws-g work — not mine to merge. Worth knowing: the shared ports made two of my verification runs fail against a *stale* server serving old code, which is why I moved to private ports.
